summary: A sound, low-risk stage-4 gate: put Marlin back where it has won every within-run comparison (turn_1) or tied (turn_4), and keep stage-3 Triton BLOCK_T 256 at T=16384, where it is about 25% faster than Marlin. The one real build hazard is tensor aliasing between the two banks in prepare(). With prefill on its last check, close it by cloning the inputs to _marlin_bank and running the Triton bank and its self-check first.
justification: Mechanism: SGLang's baseline is the same Marlin kernel. At T<=4096 the paired ratio against SGLang should therefore return to ~1.00, the parity run's 1.007/1.009 (turn_1) and 1.002/1.003 (turn_4). The turn_1 evidence is strong and consistent. Triton was 0.935/0.952 vs SGLang in stage 2 (00148fbe…) and 0.932/0.943 in stage 3 (b33b87b5), with kernel rows 796/823 and 847/729 us against Marlin's 730/681. At ~24 rows per local expert, the per-tile in-register dequant cannot amortize. The turn_4 evidence is the weakest link and is a near-tie, not a measured crossover. In stage 2, byte-identical Triton code was 1.012/0.999 vs SGLang (kernel 2158/2100 us, below Marlin's 2248/2201). In stage 3 the same code was 0.973/0.981 (2275/2318 us). The hypothesis's 'Triton loses at T=3012' leans on the second run only. The two Triton runs average ~0.99 against Marlin's ~1.00, so sending turn_4 to Marlin is the safe choice (a guaranteed ~1.0 floor), but expect +0-2.5% there, not a clear win. Cross-run kernel comparisons are noisier than LESSONS' '~1%' claim, because every run draws new routing seeds, so expert imbalance changes. The same Triton code moved +5%/+10% at turn_4 and -11% at full turn_1 between stages 2 and 3. Read this stage on the within-run paired ratio vs SGLang per shape, which is self-calibrating here because both sides run Marlin at T<=4096. Do not read it on kernel-µs against the parity profile. The 4096 bound is consistent with TASK: turn_1 T=753, turn_4 T=3012 and all five tests (max T=4096) go to Marlin, and the four first_turn shapes (T=16384) go to Triton. The headline estimate is understated. With load-geomean (0.935·0.975·1.17)^(1/3)≈1.022 today, returning turn_1 to ~1.005 and turn_4 to ~1.0 while first_turn holds ~1.17 gives ≈1.055-1.06, not 1.04. As a rewrite milestone: (1) correctness at T<=4096 is the parity path that already passed; (2) turn shapes at or below the incumbent by construction; (3) floor distance is unchanged (Marlin is 2.8x/1.4x the floor at turn_1 sliding/full), so this stage reaches 'promotable', not 'near floor'. Memory (+~0.86 GiB) and prepare time are non-issues.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity: no confound. The restored _experts_marlin is that hypothesis's own code, verbatim, and everything around the experts is byte-identical. Its run is the reference for what turn shapes should read (~1.00 vs SGLang).

experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256: no confound on the T=16384 shapes, where the code is byte-identical (only reached through the new gate). Its T<=4096 configs become unreachable, so turn-shape movement cannot come from them. Residual interaction is limited to prepare(): its bank aliases weights[*_sf/_gs] through .contiguous(), so an in-place change by prepare_moe_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin would corrupt the Triton path (see open_questions).
interference: No companion is warranted. Both outcomes read unambiguously without one. At turn shapes both sides of the paired ratio run the same Marlin kernel, so anything other than ~1.00±drift means a wiring bug in the gate (e.g., the wrong bank or block size), not an interaction. At first_turn the kernel row should match stage 3's 8574/8535/7960/8722 us within routing drift, and the shape ratio should match 1.19/1.19/1.14/1.11. An ab-revert of stage 3 would just recreate stage 2 or parity, which are already measured. A control isolating the turn_4 half of the gate (MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS=1024) would resolve a ~1-2% effect that one run cannot resolve anyway. It is not worth a check with prefill at 1 check left. Leave it for a later stage if turn_4 is tuned.
rules_flags: None blocking. The gate branches on x.shape[0] (a shape), which the rules allow. Both banks are lossless repacks of the same NVFP4 weights (Marlin repack and nibble reorder), with dequant in registers, no BF16 copy and nothing cached from data. Printing torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() in prepare() is untimed and fine. Do not add any print inside kernel_fn.
Keep any new prepare() self-check built from weights or synthetic tensors only, never from a data/Inputs sample.
open_questions: Aliasing (build must address it): master's _expert_bank stores weights['w13_sf'/'w13_gs'/'w2_sf'/'w2_gs'].contiguous(), which is the same storage as the weights. Parity's _marlin_bank hands the same aliased tensors to prepare_moe_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin. Its source is not available on this node, so whether it mutates scales or global scales in place cannot be verified. If it does, the Triton bank's scales change silently. _check_expert_gemms would not catch it, because it reads sf/gs from the bank, not from the weights. The failure would then surface only at the first_turn timed calls, burning the last check. Cheap fix: pass .clone() tensors into _marlin_bank. Also build state['bank'] and run _check_expert_gemms before _marlin_bank, and assert torch.equal on the four scale tensors before and after.

Is the prepare() self-check enough, given that no pre-timing test reaches T>4096? Mostly yes. It compiles and checks the BLOCK_T 256 variant's dequant, indexing, -1 and past-n_padded handling. The first_turn path is byte-identical to stage 3, which passed timed-call correctness at T=16384, and every timed call is checked against the reference, so a bug fails loudly rather than scoring. What it does not cover is the new wiring: which bank _experts_triton reads, and moe_align_block_size at cfg BLOCK_T on the >4096 branch. Recommended additional untimed check: one end-to-end call each of _experts_triton and _experts_marlin on a synthetic T=8192 case (random bf16 x, random top-8 local ids and weights, all built in prepare), asserting relative L2 between them below ~1e-2. That covers the aliasing hazard and the branch wiring for a few hundred ms.
Make sure _experts' dispatch reads x.shape[0] (= config tokens), not num_slots, and that the Marlin branch uses state['marlin'] for the bank and workspace while the Triton branch uses state['bank'].
T between 4096 and 16384 is untuned and unscored, so the crossover there is unknown. That is acceptable, but note it in FINDINGS so a later turn_4 stage does not assume 4096 was measured.
